decisions.decision: The Runner reports exactly two of the five coordinate groups in docs/operations/self-update.md section 5.1: binary (version, binary_sha256) and canonical schema interval (schema_min, schema_max). It does not report contract_release, contract_digest, runner_api_min, runner_api_max, bundle_digest, candidate_id, key_id or algorithm, and no placeholder or empty field for them is added.
decisions.rationale: Measured. internal/update/update.go:26-34 declares Manifest with exactly Schema, Version, OS, Architecture, BinarySHA256, SchemaMin and SchemaMax, so the binary and schema-interval coordinates are values a running binary genuinely carries; cmd/runner/main.go:13 carries const version = "0.1.0-dev", a real value. A search for runner_api, contract_release, contract_digest, ContractRelease and RunnerAPI across every *.go, *.yaml and *.json in the tree finds them only in docs/operations/self-update.md and in .agents/v2/evidence/V2-033-update.json: no code produces them. A report field for a coordinate no binary carries could only be filled by inventing a value at the report site, which is the exact shape of the failure non_goal 1 forbids -- a self-claim treated as if it were a measurement. Section 5.1 item 2 also states that the schema interval is the coexist mechanism and not a validation detail, and section 6's invariant is written over intervals alone, so the interval is the one coordinate the invariant actually consumes. OS and architecture are excluded for the opposite reason: they are real values but no rule reads them, and adding them would widen the aggregate past the version-and-compatibility question (non_goal 2). contract, bundle and provenance become additive optional fields later, owned by V2-034 for the manifest fields and V2-074 for the compatibility decision; that is recorded, not pre-built.

decisions.decision: The reporting path is one additive optional object on the existing runner-authenticated heartbeat. POST /v1/runner/heartbeat gains runner_version: {version, binary_sha256, schema_min, schema_max}. No new endpoint, no change to enrollment, no new authenticator, no new idempotency story.
decisions.rationale: Enrollment is rejected as the carrier on a measured argument, not a preference: enrollment happens once per Runner identity (internal/runner/protocol.go:71 IssueEnrollment, consumed once at ChallengePath) while the binary is switched many times per identity -- section 5.2 has installed.json record every switch with its reason. A version captured at enrollment is therefore permanently stale after the first self-update, and would report the version the machine ran when it enrolled: precisely the reading section 6 must not be given. The per-Execution requests are rejected for a second measured reason: POST /v1/executions/{id}:start and POST /v1/executions/result only occur when the machine has work, and the mixed-version window of section 6 is exactly the period in which a machine may be idle, so those paths can go silent for the whole interval the invariant is about. Heartbeat is the only recurring Runner-to-Control-Plane request (internal/api/api.go:302), already carries the runnerSession scheme, already runs through the idempotency path, and already writes a per-Runner record (internal/application/service.go:460 SaveRunnerObservation). contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml:317-321 sets additionalProperties:false on HeartbeatRequest and internal/api/api.go:781 sets DisallowUnknownFields, so the field cannot be introduced informally and an unknown field is still a 400. Consequence recorded rather than hidden: requestFingerprint("heartbeat", req) at service.go:393 covers the whole request, so replaying one request_id with a changed report is ErrIdempotencyConflict -- unchanged existing semantics, and a Runner already needs a fresh request_id per heartbeat.

decisions.decision: The report is stored in a side table keyed by RunnerID (RunnerVersionReportRepository, a new port on UnitOfWork). No Runner aggregate is created, no field is added to domain.RunnerObservation, and internal/domain is not edited at all by this task.
decisions.rationale: Two precedents point the same way. internal/application/ports.go:181-188 makes ControlRequestedByRepository a side table keyed by Control Intent revision because domain.ControlIntent is proven-closed M1 surface, and dp-v2-067 d7 put the Provider assignment in an Execution-keyed side table for the same reason. A version report has no state transition, no Version, and no invariant that domain.Validate or domain.Permit consults, so it is not an aggregate. Putting it on domain.RunnerObservation (internal/domain/control.go:54-63) was measured and rejected for a specific, decisive reason: that record is rewritten in full on every heartbeat (service.go:460 constructs a fresh value), so a heartbeat that omitted the report would overwrite a previously reported version with zero values, destroying exactly the reported-versus-not-reported distinction non_goal 3 exists to protect. It would also put binary-distribution vocabulary inside the one package whose source guard exists to keep outside-world concepts out (internal/domain/source_guard_test.go), and would move the domain component key for a value no domain rule reads.

decisions.decision: One bounded enumeration port is added, for the version report only: RunnerVersionReports(ctx, limit) returning at most MaxRunnerVersionReports entries in a fixed order. RunnerObservationRepository is not widened.
decisions.rationale: The cross-machine invariant is a statement over every machine, so a per-key lookup cannot express it and no enumeration exists today: internal/application/repository.go:548 records the measured fact verbatim -- "RunnerObservationRepository is keyed by a single runner id with no enumeration port". Widening the observation repository instead would widen a surface the reconciler and the control-verification path already read, for no gain, since the intersection needs only the intervals. The enumeration is bounded by a declared constant because machines are not shared (section 5.2) so the Runner count is the machine count, not a function of Requirement count -- which is what keeps docs/architecture/validation.md section 5's growth rules satisfiable and is why no cursor or page_size is introduced.

decisions.decision: A Runner's own claim is never authority over what that Runner may read. Authentication and authorization stay exactly as they are: the runner session and the role decide, and no code path in the request-admission chain reads the report. This is proven two ways -- an AST scan asserting that internal/api/auth.go and application's runnerCaller/callerActor path reference neither the report type nor the port, and a behavioural test in which a Runner whose reported interval excludes every plausible canonical schema still succeeds unchanged at claim, permit, start, result, heartbeat and checkpoint.
decisions.rationale: non_goal 1, made mechanical. The session proves which Runner spoke; it proves nothing about whether the sentence is true. Turning the claim into a read gate would let a merely mis-built binary -- not even a hostile one -- widen or narrow its own access by changing a build constant, and would make the control plane's access decision depend on a value it cannot check. The honest uses of an unverifiable claim are to report it and to refuse to advance on it; permitting is not one of them. The behavioural half of the proof matters more than the scan: a scan can be satisfied by indirection, whereas a Runner that keeps working with a deliberately absurd reported interval demonstrates the absence of the coupling.

decisions.decision: What the Control Plane does verify is shape, not truth, and it says so. Validation: version matches the same semver shape internal/update/update.go:23 pins; binary_sha256 is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters; schema_min is at least 1; schema_max is at least schema_min; both are at or below a declared numeric ceiling; and the object is all-present or wholly absent -- a partial object is 400 and stores nothing. reported_at on the stored record is the transaction's authority time, never a Runner-supplied timestamp, and the request object carries no timestamp field at all.
decisions.rationale: internal/application/service.go:426-427 already states the rule for this exact class of value -- "Runner clocks and caller-provided timestamps are not authoritative" -- and enforces it by overwriting every ProcessObservation.At with authorityAt; the report follows that rule rather than inventing a second one, and omitting the field from the request makes a Runner clock structurally unable to enter the record. Refusing a partial object is the load-bearing part: an object carrying schema_max with no schema_min would otherwise be stored as an interval starting at zero, which reads as wider than anything the machine can actually do, and a too-wide interval is the one error that makes the intersection look non-empty when it is not. Nothing here checks that the claim is true, and the design states that plainly rather than implying otherwise: internal/update.Verify runs on the Runner machine against bytes the control plane never receives, so no control-plane code can confirm a version.

decisions.decision: Not-reported, stale and invalid are three separate first-class values, and the derived answer has an explicit unknown. report_state is a closed enum {reported, not-reported, stale}; the interval and the binary coordinates are present in the view only when report_state is reported, so there is no default interval anywhere. The intersection view carries intersection_state in {non-empty, empty, unknown} and is unknown whenever any enumerated Runner is not in state reported. No field or enum value spells compatible without unknown being a sibling value, and a table test fails if a constant is added without a case or a case without a constant.
decisions.rationale: non_goal 3, and the measured present state makes it the common case rather than an edge: today zero Runners report anything, so a design whose default reads as compatible would be wrong about every machine on the day it ships. Staleness must be distinct from absence because a Runner that reported and then stopped heart-beating is a different operational fact from one that never reported, and only the first tells an operator that a machine went quiet. The explicit unknown is what makes section 6's refusal sound: "an advance that would empty the intersection is refused, not scheduled" is only a real refusal if I-do-not-know cannot be silently rounded to non-empty.

decisions.decision: The intersection is computed and reported; nothing is gated on it, and this task introduces no canonical schema counter and no advance operation.
decisions.rationale: Measured: currentSchema exists only as a parameter of update.Verify and update.Install (internal/update/update.go:41, :71). No constant, field, record or store anywhere in the repository owns the canonical schema value, so there is nothing to compare an intersection against and no operation whose refusal would consume it. Introducing the counter here would make a reporting task the owner of the value V2-070's four-stage migration advances and V2-034 reads, which puts a migration decision inside a surface change. The input to the invariant is what this task owes; the refusal that consumes it belongs to whoever owns the advance. That split is recorded as an escalation with a named owner instead of being closed by invention.

decisions.decision: The observable surface is GET /v1/runners, owner-role only, bounded by the enumeration constant, declared in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml with additionalProperties:false, plus a self-contained Runners block appended to internal/web/owner.html and internal/web/owner.js under a V2-069 marker comment.
decisions.rationale: No existing owner path enumerates Runners: the GET routes at internal/api/api.go:133-209 cover /owner, /v1/requirements, /v1/controls, /v1/requirements/{id} and /v1/repositories only. Folding the report into /v1/queue/summary was rejected because that response is V2-068's surface and both tasks would then edit the same schema block, converting a scheduling question into a merge conflict. The collection is bounded by construction -- machines are not shared, so the row count is the machine count -- which is why no cursor or page_size is added; MaxPageSize and cursors exist for collections that grow. Both console files are effectively single-line minified documents, so an appended, marker-commented, self-contained block is the only edit shape that does not rewrite unrelated bytes.

decisions.decision: The Runner-side code that fills the field is out of scope, and the evidence must say so. Measured: cmd/runner/main.go:28-30 refuses to run without --fake with the message "runner: no external control-plane wiring is enabled", and a search for net/http across internal/runner returns nothing -- there is no heartbeat client anywhere in the repository. V2-069 builds and exercises the accept, validate, store and report path through the API with a runner session, exactly as internal/api's existing runner tests do, and does not edit cmd/**.
decisions.rationale: Honesty about what the record may claim. Publishing a report field and then describing the outcome as though production Runners were populating it would be the same class of error as the static schema_version:"v1" this task exists to replace: a surface that reads as informative while knowing nothing. Keeping cmd/** out of allowed_paths also keeps the runner and control-plane component keys from moving for a change that does not touch them.

decisions.decision: The report object carries four scalar fields and nothing else. There is no message, detail, hostname, ip, host, path, root, env or free-text field on the request DTO, the port type, the stored record or the read model, so a machine identifier beyond the already-authenticated RunnerID is structurally unrepresentable rather than filtered. Asserted by an AST field-name scan over the new types plus the credential-shape deny list internal/domain/source_guard_test.go already declares.
decisions.rationale: internal/provider.WorkPacket and internal/runner.ProviderRequest established this construction in this repository -- the guarantee is that there is no field to put the value in, so no redaction step can be forgotten -- and dp-v2-067 d12 reused it. A version report is a natural place for someone to later attach a hostname or an install path for debugging; making those unrepresentable now is cheaper than removing them later, and a machine's identity is already carried by the session.

decisions.decision: ci/components.json is not edited and no new import edge is created. The report DTO is a plain struct in internal/application with no import of internal/update: the semver shape and the digest shape are re-declared locally as literals. A test in internal/application pins the two shapes against a literal accept/reject table copied by value from internal/update's pattern, with no import of internal/update in production or test code.
decisions.rationale: ci/components.json declares application's dependencies as [domain, infra]; api, store-memory and store-firestore already declare application. Importing internal/update from internal/application would create an application-to-update edge, and internal/ci's manifest derivation reads test imports as well as production imports, so even a test-only import would move the declared DAG -- which V2-045 owns and which is not editable here. The cost of re-declaring is that the two patterns can drift, so the mitigation is named rather than assumed: a literal table, pinned in a test whose name says what it pins. Recorded note for V2-045 under gate rule G6: this task moves the application, api, store-memory, store-firestore, web, contracts and docs component keys, and editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts key, a declared contract dependency of the api and control-plane components.

decisions.decision: V2-069 belongs to the surface-widening serialization chain and should be inserted immediately after V2-066, giving V2-064 (complete) to V2-066 to V2-069 to V2-067 to V2-068 to V2-065. Issuing the id and recording the position is the coordinator's.
decisions.rationale: The task touches five of the six files the chain exists to serialize: internal/api/api.go, internal/application/{ports,service,readmodels}.go, contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, internal/web/owner.{html,js} and both store adapters. It cannot avoid the chain by dropping the read surface, because the heartbeat handler, the ports and the openapi request schema are already three of those files. Position is chosen on the dependency facts: V2-069 depends only on V2-016 (complete) and has no dependency on V2-067, V2-068 or V2-065, while V2-035 -- the M8 task whose completion condition this feeds -- depends on V2-069, so putting it last would serialize a milestone branch behind four unrelated surface tasks. Its openapi and read-model additions are disjoint from the Provider registry (V2-067) and the queue summary (V2-068), so landing it early minimises the merge surface for the three tasks that follow rather than increasing it.

risks: No Runner in this repository posts a heartbeat: cmd/runner/main.go refuses to run without --fake and internal/runner contains no net/http. Every assertion is therefore driven through the API with a runner session, and the evidence must state that the production report count is zero at completion. A record that implies otherwise is worse than no record.

The intersection has no consumer, because no canonical schema counter exists (update.go:41, :71 pass currentSchema in as a parameter). A reader may take a reported non-empty intersection as proof that an advance is safe. The mitigation is that the view reports endpoints and state only, names no advance, and the documentation states that the refusal belongs to the task that owns the advance.

Adding a field to HeartbeatRequest changes requestFingerprint's input, so a client that replays one request_id with a changed report now gets ErrIdempotencyConflict. This is existing semantics, not new behaviour, but it must be asserted deliberately and recorded, because a heartbeat loop that reused request ids would surface it as a new failure.

The semver and digest shapes are re-declared in internal/application rather than imported from internal/update, to avoid creating an application-to-update edge that only V2-045 may declare. The two declarations can drift; the literal pinning table is the only thing that will catch it, and the design note must say so plainly.

Editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts component key and is a declared contract dependency of the api and control-plane components. Only the application and api evidence records are issued here; the remaining key movement is a measured note for V2-045 under gate rule G6.

This task is in the surface-widening chain and shares six files with V2-066, V2-067, V2-068 and V2-065. If it is scheduled concurrently with any of them the conflict is in the openapi schema block and the owner console, both of which are append-only in this design; that reduces but does not remove the cost, so the serialization must be respected rather than relied on to be harmless.
